correctness.rationale: The path Laplacian mean-zero rank-one formula yields delta K=nt S/(1+td). Solving Lx=e_i-e_j gives a centered integer ramp; direct summation gives S=C_n(d)-d^2(l-r)^2/(4n). Parity-mismatched d>=3 loses strictly to a neighboring symmetric chord by numerator arithmetic averaging with exactly matching denominator averages. For even n, d=2 loses strictly to d=3 by the exact positive S and S/d differences. For symmetric lengths, the adjacent gain comparison has an explicit single positive threshold t_d iff 4d>3n+4. The continuous normalized gain has positive derivative up to 3n/4 and thereafter strictly decreasing derivative numerator, forcing strictly unimodal sampled maxima, no skipped lengths and at most one adjacent tied pair. The independent grounded-Laplacian Fraction inversion in verify.py reproduces all optimal chord sets and values in 1,587 finite graph/weight checks; the infinite claim rests on these symbolic inequalities, not enumeration.

Seven meaning-based research-record searches of source/parameters/equivalent phrasing found only conceptually adjacent, noncovering records. value.rationale: One fixed-conductance shortcut placement on a path is a natural minimal graph design problem and the Kirchhoff index is a recognized whole-network resistance/consensus metric. The result supplies an all-size, all-weight exact optimum, a structural exclusion of every asymmetric placement, a discrete sequence of sharp rational conductance transitions, and the unexpected onset only at n=9; these are useful as benchmark instances and describe a real design change. They are not just a numeric check or arbitrary finite table.
